title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 6: Augustine — elect makes rich in faith as he makes heirs
pass_a_gloss: Finally, for a fuller understanding of the words let this also be added: although God does not elect men from foresight of faith, he is rightly said to have chosen those rich in faith, because in time he makes such all those whom he elected from eternity; and because, having made them such, he already actually and as it were visibly elects them, and transfers them, set apart from unbelievers, into his own peculiar people. Let us close this reply with those words by which Augustine explained this very place: God chose the faithful, but that they might become so, not because they already were. By electing, therefore, he makes them rich in faith, just as he makes them heirs of the kingdom. Rightly indeed is this choosing said in them, that what he may do in them, he chose them. So he, On the Predestination of the Saints, book 1, chapter 17.
pass_b_english: Add this for the full sense: God does not elect from foresight of faith, yet he is rightly said to have chosen the rich in faith — because in time he makes such everyone he elected from eternity; and because, once made such, he already actually and almost visibly elects them, sets them apart from unbelievers, and takes them as his own. Close with Augustine on this very text (On the Predestination of the Saints 1.17): "God chose the faithful, but that they might become so, not because they already were. By electing he makes them rich in faith, just as he makes them heirs of the kingdom." That choosing is rightly said of them: he chose them so that he might do this in them.
source_text: Denique ad pleniorem verborum intelligentiam accedat & hoc quoque; Quamvis Deus non eligat homines ex praescientia fidei, recte tamen dicitur elegisse divites in fide, quia tales facit in tempore eos omnes, quos elegit ab aeterno; & quia tales factos jam actualiter & quasi visibiliter eligit, & ab infidelibus secretos in peculium suum transfert. Concludamus hoc responsum verbis illis quibus Augustinus hunc ipsum locum explicavit; Elegit Deus fideles, sed ut fiant, non quia jam erant. Eligendo ergo facit divites in fide, sicut heredes regni. Recte quippe in eis hoc eligere dicitur, quod ut in eis faciat, eos elegit. Haec ille, De Praedest. Sanct. lib. 1. cap. 17.
